newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Compass upbeat about future.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Compass upbeat about future.

text.p: British catering company Compass Group Plc is confident it can continue to sustain its current growth rate, said managing director Roger Matthews.

"We are basically very confident of continuing our underlying growth rate," said Matthews in an interview, shortly after Compass posted an 18 percent increase in half year profits to 56.4 million stg. The group has achieved an eightfold increase in turnover since 1992 to 2.65 billion at year end 1996 while profits quadrupled over the same period.
"We have successfully built up the business over the years and we are now competing with a solid base in each of the international markets."
Matthews said he expected major companies to continue outsourcing their catering.
In Britain Compass picked up accounts with British Nuclear Fuels, Siemens and a 10 year deal with concert venue the Belfast Waterfront Hall.
In the United States, which showed profits growth of 20 percent to 17.8 million in the half year, outsourcing was especially strong in the healthcare and education foodservice markets.
The U.S. division won catering contracts with the Louisiana State University for 26,000 students and annual turnover of 6.6 million stg.
In mainland Europe, where profits grew 35 percent to 38 million stg, the group won a contract with Mercedes-Benz for 1,600 staff at five sites, with Villeroy & Boch and Commerzbank Plaza.

"Clearly pressure is on companies to reduce costs and concentrate on their core businesses, and leave catering to the experts and I see no reason why that trend won't continue for many years to come."
He estimates about two thirds of the group's market -- companies, schools and hospitals -- will remain self-catering until the year 2000.
Margins continued to improve, rising from 4 percent to 4.3 percent in the United States, 3.9 percent to 4.1 percent in mainland Europe.

"We see gradual consistent margin improvement coming through from the main divisions," said Matthews. The group has set longer term targets for margins, to be achieved over the coming years, at 7-7.5 percent in Britain, 5.0-5.5 percent in the United States and 6.0-6.5 percent in mainland Europe.
Margins have also been lifted by the introduction of two brands into outlets -- Uppercrust, filled baquettes made by Compass on site, and Ritazza coffee.
